title: Hard mismatch: immediate move-in and 4 bedrooms

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: I need to move in next month and need four bedrooms. Any unit?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Pearlmont Phase 1 only has 3-bedroom units, and completion is expected in Q4 2029, so it wouldn’t suit a move-in next month or a 4-bedroom requirement. Are either of those requirements flexible?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: No, both are must-haves for me, so Pearlmont won’t work. Thanks for clarifying.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Understood—if both are must-haves, Pearlmont isn’t the right fit. Thanks for clarifying, and I hope you find a place that suits your move-in timing and space needs.

retrieval_trace.trigger_message: I need to move in next month and need four bedrooms. Any unit?
No, both are must-haves for me, so Pearlmont won’t work. Thanks for clarifying.

what_moved_buyer_forward: The AI promptly stated the bedroom-count and completion-timing mismatch.
It checked whether either stated requirement was flexible before closing the conversation.
what_reduced_conversion_probability: Pearlmont did not meet either of the buyer’s confirmed hard requirements; an appointment would not have been commercially appropriate.
conversion_analysis.where_conversion_was_won_or_lost: No Pearlmont conversion was viable. The AI correctly established the mismatch, accepted the buyer’s answer, and did not pressure them into a viewing or invent alternatives.

what_agent_did_well: Recognized both hard-fit blockers immediately and communicated the supported facts clearly.
Asked one relevant question to check flexibility without unnecessary personal qualification.
Accepted the buyer’s firm answer and ended politely without pushing a viewing.
judge.better_next_move: No material change needed. The respectful close was appropriate after the buyer confirmed both requirements were non-negotiable.

recommended_improvement.reason: The AI handled this case well. As a general guidance enhancement, make the stop-selling rule explicit when a buyer confirms that a hard requirement is incompatible with the project.

judge.summary: The AI accurately identified a hard mismatch: the buyer needs four bedrooms and next-month move-in, while Pearlmont’s supplied facts indicate three-bedroom units and expected Q4 2029 completion. It confirmed the requirements were inflexible, then closed without pushing an appointment or escalating unnecessarily. No conversion was appropriate.
